Subject: Post-demo: Hosted evaluation path & deployment fit questions

Hi Raj / Alice —

Thanks again for taking time today. Quick recap of what we covered and a suggested next-step path so RetailX can evaluate Hosted API quickly while we size the need for Dedicated or Private: 

What we demoed
- Hosted API for fast evaluation: REST/SDK endpoints, streaming, and per-route dashboards.
- Rate-limit examples and how we surface token-level cost in the console.
- Dedicated / Private options if you need sustained high throughput or VPC isolation.

Recommendation for a 2-week Hosted evaluation (goal: validate latency, integration work, and cost profile)
1) Provision test keys (we can create a sandbox org on Hosted).
2) Run the two sample workloads in sample_payloads.json (attached) at low concurrency to validate latency and outputs.
3) Use the attached sample-rate-limit-profile.csv to exercise burst and sustained rates.
4) Share a small prompt set for quality checks; we'll run evals and report regressions.

Quick technical notes
- Endpoints: POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate and https://api.redwood.ai/v1/chat for streaming.
- Default sandbox rate limits: 60 requests/minute, 20 concurrent streams (can be raised for pilot).
- Token pricing and streaming behavior will be visible in the console; we can provide token-slicing guidance for cost sensitivity.

Next steps I propose
- If you're comfortable, I can provision sandbox keys and an initial trial org by tomorrow.
- Vivek: can you confirm concurrency guidance and any recommended request shaping for RetailX's catalog use-case?
- Raj: send estimated qps and average prompt/response token sizes so we can model cost and latency.

Attachments: redwood_hosted_quickstart_onepager.pdf; sample-rate-limit-profile.csv; sample_payloads.json

Thanks, Tessa — great demo. A couple of clarifying items from our side before we kick off sandbox testing: 

1) Rate limits and burst behavior — we expect bursts up to ~450 rps for short windows (30s) during promotions, steady-state 40–60 rps. How does the Hosted sandbox handle short bursts above the default?

2) Concurrency and streaming: Some endpoints will stream product descriptions as they generate; can we sustain 20+ concurrent streams for the longer responses (avg 800 tokens)?

3) Data handling: RetailX will be sending SKU-level inventory and some PII-adjacent customer identifiers. Does Hosted retain request/response content by default and what are deletion/retention options for the trial?

I'll attach our rough traffic profile following today's call and a sample prompt. If Hosted needs to be bumped for capacity I'm open to a short Dedicated trial if it proves necessary, but we'd prefer Hosted for speed to value unless isolation is required.

-Raj

Subject: Re: Post-demo: Hosted evaluation path & deployment fit questions

Hi Raj — quick answers to the three questions; happy to jump on a short call if you want to walk through numbers.

1) Bursts: Hosted supports burst capacity beyond default rate limits via autoscaling and request queuing for short windows. For 450 rps bursts we typically recommend a pilot configuration bump (we can raise sandbox burst cap to 1k rps for a short window while we monitor). There are two levers: per-key rate-limit raise and transient burst policy at the org level.

2) Concurrency & streaming: 20 concurrent streams of ~800 tokens each is realistic on Hosted for short pilots, but cost and latency depend on your average sequence length and top-p settings. We recommend enabling prefix/KV caching on repeated SKU prompts and using streaming backpressure to manage client-side timeouts. If you need guaranteed sustained concurrency (e.g., 24/7 200+ concurrent workers) Dedicated is a better fit.

3) Data retention: By default Hosted retains request/response logs for 30 days for debugging, but you can opt out for your org or set shorter retention windows. For trial orgs handling PII-like identifiers we can enable request-only hashing and immediate retention override; for regulated workloads Private (VPC/on-prem) is the recommended path. We will document retention settings and provide a summary SOC2-compatible evidence packet for your security team.

Operational suggestions for the evaluation
- Start with 0.5–1.0 qps per worker from a small fleet and gradually ramp to simulate burst with a traffic-replay approach.
- Use token-slicing and streaming to reduce end-to-end latency for long outputs.
- We'll instrument cost estimates in the Console; share actual prompt sizes and we will produce an estimated monthly spend at different concurrency bands.

I'll provision a sandbox rate-limit raise for the first 48 hours once Tessa confirms.

-Vivek
